## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kummāsapiṇḍijātaka* (Ja 415) is a narrative belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. Set at Jetavana, the frame story concerns Queen Mallikā, who had been the daughter of the chief garland-maker of Sāvatthī and was renowned for her beauty and goodness [SuttaCentral]. According to the prologue to the Jātaka cited in modern scholarship, Mallikā had originally been a poor flower girl whom King Pasenadi encountered by chance following a military defeat, leading him to fall in love with her, marry her, and appoint her his chief queen [Bodhi 2003]. Four modern translations in four languages are registered on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse analyses via DharmaNexus identify extensive Pali-internal correspondence between the *Kummāsapiṇḍijātaka* and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Tatiyo bhāgo), encompassing twelve matching passages (the longest spanning §3.4–7.4) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus detects matches with Āryaśūra's Sanskrit *Jātakamālā* and its Tibetan translation (D4150) [DharmaNexus].
